answer:
Natural-language answer (data-grounded hypothesis): "On average, original papers in Experimental Economics are about 28.0 pages long (mean = 28.00, N = 18 original papers; median 27.5, SD 7.37, range 16–45), whereas original papers in Psychology are about 11.2 pages long (mean = 11.22, N = 97 original papers from the Reproducibility Project: Psychology; median 9, SD 6.30, range 1–31). Experimental Economics originals are therefore roughly 2.5 times longer than Psychology originals."

Final computed values (from meta-regression_study_data_heterogeneity_in_replication_projects.csv):
- Experimental Economics (project=='ee', validated 1:1 with discipline=='Economics'): mean = 28.00 pages, N = 18, median = 27.5, SD = 7.37, min/max = 16/45.
- Psychology (project=='rpp'): mean = 11.2165 pages, N = 97, median = 9.0, SD = 6.30, min/max = 1/31.

Diagnostics:
- 0 missing / 0 zero lengths in target groups; no imputation needed.
- Unit of analysis: each original paper's id is unique within ee (18/18) and rpp (97/97); dedup by id gives identical means.
- Sensitivity — dedup by title: ee unchanged (18, 28.00); rpp becomes N=95, mean=11.232 (two RPP papers were entered twice, each pair with identical length: Albarracin et al. JPSP 2008 = 14 pp., Bressan & Stranieri PS 2008 = 7 pp.); both rpp variants round to 11.2, so the answer is unchanged at report precision.
- Cross-check: the second file lists Experimental Economics=18 (matching ee) but Psychology=73 — a smaller meta-regression 'replication success' subset lacking a length column; per approval, it does not alter the computation (primary rpp population N=97 from the first file).

payload.workflow: Loaded primary study dataset (927x57); filtered project in {ee, rpp} (115 rows); cross-validated ee==discipline Economics (identical sets); verified 0 missing/0 zero lengths and unique ids per group; computed group mean/median/SD/min/max of length; ran sensitivity checks dedup-by-id (identical) and dedup-by-title (rpp 95/11.232); cross-checked naming vs second replication-success file (no length column); reported final means 28.0 (EE, N=18) and 11.2 (Psychology, N=97)
